title: Information and communication going global
content:
1. In 1989, a British scientist at a physics laboratory in Switzerland published a technical paper that would change the world. The title of Professor Tim Berners-Lee's paper was "Information Management: A Proposal." It introduced the world to Berners-Lee's brainchild – the World Wide Web – a system for publishing information over the Internet. The world's first-ever website went "live" on December 20, 1990. Eight months later on August 6, 1991, the World Wide Web made its Internet debut. The World Wide Web made easy access to the Internet possible. Few people could have imagined the changes this easy access to the Internet would bring about.

2. Thanks to the Web we can chat with others and make friends with people from all over the world without stepping foot outside the front door. Facebook, the social networking service, was founded in 2004 and now has an estimated two billion users; Tencent's WeChat has over one billion users. Keeping in touch globally has never been easier and cheaper. For business people, LinkedIn helps create opportunities for job seekers to network and job providers to find potential employees. The Internet has removed all barriers to communication.

3. Want to share your opinions or get the opinions of others? Start your own Weibo. Post your thoughts on Twitter as long as your message is 280 characters or less. Want to buy a smartphone and you're not sure which one will best meet your need? Find an opinion leader on the Web, or locate a website that makes those comparisons for you. Sharing opinions online also means we are no longer limited to traditional news media or authorities for information and opinions.

4. Perhaps the biggest commercial revolution made possible by the World Wide Web is e-commerce, the ability to buy and sell online. One can order lunch sitting on the sofa at home or sell Chinese-made electronics in California. We can make global travel arrangements online, and even secure visas to enter some countries online. Need something to help you to relax? Find an online game and play with gamers from around the world. Want to hear the latest music? Download music from Apple's iTunes. How do we pay for these goods and services? Through the Internet, of course.

5. The spread of Internet access in the past was limited because everyone needed a PC to connect to the Web. On June 29, 2007, all that changed when Apple introduced the first smartphone to consumers. Since smartphones are less expensive than computers, they can be found nearly everywhere across the globe including rural villages far away from the city. Take the Chinese farmers who connected to markets throughout the country using the Internet. Before they were able to sell their apples online, 90 percent of their apples rotted and could not be sold.

6. Smartphones have made new methods of retail payment possible. Instead of using cash or a credit card, we need only wave our phone over a scanner thanks to innovations such as Alipay, WeChat Pay and Apple Pay. Banking online is now international. Need to transfer money from your bank account in New York to your friend's account at the China Construction Bank? No problem. We have an app for that, too.

7. A world of information and communication possibilities is now at our fingertips all thanks to Professor Tim Berners-Lee. Even he could not have imagined the changes that the World Wide Web has made possible.
